## Components and authority

| Component | Responsibility | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Owner dashboard | Wallet session, agent configuration, approvals, monitoring | Authenticated UI; never asks for the owner's seed phrase |
| Control service | Policies, scheduler, atomic reservations, audit events, revocation epochs; the owner's sealed model key and model calls; browse permits; connector calls; result delivery; swap approval | Single authority for workspace/agent/task spending allowances; agents receive completions and fenced data, never keys |
| Agent runner | Bounded planning, catalog selection, requesting purchases, reading permitted public pages in a cookie-less Chrome context, saving outputs | No note database, provider key, reference image, arbitrary signer or policy mutation |
| Wallet service | Encrypted notes, local proofs, constrained fresh-wallet signing, recovery | Checks current policy before releasing financial authority |
| Relayer / indexer | Sponsor permitted chain costs, submit withdrawals, co-sign the one permitted devnet swap shape, rebuild public tree state | Does not receive note secrets; indexer cannot invent accepted roots |
| Privacy pool program | Verify proofs, conserve value, consume nullifiers, enforce bound destinations and owner exits | On-chain enforcement; PDA controls the SPL vault |
| Service gateway | Immutable quotes, settlement reconciliation, durable credits, delivery/result cache | Merchant is the gateway operator; credits stay linked to an authenticated workspace |
| x402 facilitator | Verify and settle standard exact SVM payment | Merchant leg only; distinct from the private-withdrawal relayer |
| Owner's model provider | Planning, analysis, content and reference-image style, called by control with the owner's key | Billed to the owner; sees prompts, gathered data and the reference image |
| OpenRouter / data adapter | Operator-sponsored planning trial, paid inference SKUs or explicitly labeled research data | Provider availability and commercial funding are operator dependencies |
| MCP connector servers | Read-only tools pinned by digest; CoinGecko market data through Veilo templates | Third-party text, fenced as untrusted; servers see the requested arguments |
| Orca whirlpool (devnet) | USDC to SOL for an owner-approved swap from a fresh wallet | One pinned pool; devnet prices are not market prices |

## Implemented stack and source layout

TypeScript, Next.js dashboard, Express gateway, durable workers, SQLite WAL, Rust/Anchor pool program and Circom/snarkjs BN254 Groth16 proofs. Versions are pinned in lockfiles and proof artifacts in `artifacts/circuits/manifest.json`; see [deployment](../deployment.md).

| Source path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `apps/dashboard/` | Landing page, owner/guest/public-view workspace, marketplace pages and same-origin proxy to the control API |
| `services/control/`, `services/runner/` | Policy, reservations, scheduler and restricted workers |
| `services/wallet/`, `services/relayer/` | Private state, signing, proofs and public chain adapters |
| `services/gateway/` | x402 routes, credit ledger and provider adapters; also the seller-host profile for marketplace jobs |
| `services/marketplace/`, `supabase/migrations/` | Marketplace API over Supabase Auth/Postgres/Storage and its schema/RLS |
| `packages/contracts/`, `packages/db/`, `packages/mcp-client/` | Shared schemas, migrations, durable state and the read-only MCP client |
| `packages/privacy-sdk/`, `packages/x402-client/` | Witness/encoding logic and constrained payment adapter |
| `programs/privacy-pool/`, `circuits/` | On-chain program and spend/insert/exit circuits |
| `tests/`, `scripts/`, `artifacts/` | Acceptance tests, operator commands and public artifact manifests |

These paths exist in the source snapshot. Documentation has its own dependency manifest and lockfile under `docs/`. The funded dashboard/browser-wallet flow remains **not yet run**; local UI checks are recorded separately in build status T14. The dashboard (`apps/dashboard`) serves a public landing page at `/`, the owner workspace at `/workspace` and the open marketplace under `/marketplace`.

## Marketplace extension

`services/marketplace` uses Supabase Auth, Postgres and private Storage for marketplace identity, catalogue, jobs, artifact metadata and accounting projections (19 migrations under `supabase/migrations/`). Local control retains policies/reservations/revocation and local wallet retains secrets/proofs/signing. The cloud never becomes a spending authority. It receives acknowledged state through an outbound, authenticated, digest-bound and expiring connection initiated by local control. Spending pauses while control is offline.

Marketplace Web3 sign-in and the existing local wallet challenge are deliberately separate. The local P0 stack still works without Supabase. Seller settlement goes directly to the reviewed recipient: managed listings run on the gateway's seller-host profile (`GATEWAY_ROLE=seller-host`), which pays the listing's payout address, not the operator merchant. No pool-contract change is needed solely for the extension. See the [marketplace boundary diagram](./marketplace.md) and [source-based triage](./marketplace-triage.md).

## Enforcement placement

The chain/proofs enforce ownership, approved-set membership for private spends, value conservation, nullifier uniqueness, withdrawal intent and owner exit. The wallet/control service enforces budgets, merchant selection, revocation and signing policy. The gateway enforces paid delivery, credit issuance/debit, request binding and provider cost limits. The model is not a security authority.

The devnet swap is enforced at three points: control (owner approval, maximum per swap, caps), the wallet (decodes the quoted swap before signing) and the relayer (accepts only the exact five-instruction transaction). See [payments](./payments.md#devnet-swap).

Off-chain spending caps are not proof-enforced caps. Compromise of the owner wallet service can bypass its local policy and expose its notes.

## Durable state

Control owns scoped allowance reservations; the gateway owns issued/reserved/consumed credits. Link operations across these databases with stable operation IDs and durable outbox/inbox events. Do not maintain two independently authoritative copies of the gateway balance.

Keep encrypted notes and signer/provider secrets separate from runner-readable activity. A restart must reconcile released proofs, signed transactions and provider attempts before creating new financial authority. See [payments](./payments.md) and [policy](./policy.md).

---

# Payment lifecycle

For recorded verification and remaining checks, see [current status](./status.md).

The private withdrawal and x402 merchant payment are separate transactions. A fresh payment wallet uses ordinary x402; x402 alone does not hide the source of funds.

[Diagram definition included below.]

## Before a purchase

1. Verify devnet genesis, mint owner/decimals, token program, deployment manifest and compatible proof artifacts. Reject mainnet in demo mode.
2. The owner signs a deposit. Track submitted, finalized, indexed, approved and spendable separately. Pending or unapproved notes are unavailable.
3. Control authenticates the requester, creates a stable operation and request digest, and obtains an immutable gateway quote.
4. In one atomic control transaction, check every allowance scope and reserve input note/exposure. A second agent cannot spend that same note or last available allowance.

## Private funding

The wallet service persists a fresh signer before funding it. A local real proof demonstrates note and approved-label membership, valid nullifier, range-checked value/change and an intent bound to pool/program, devnet, mint, payout account, amount, fees, relayer where applicable and expiry.

The on-chain program verifies this proof, consumes the input nullifier, transfers only the bound amount and queues private change atomically. Change becomes spendable only after authenticated insertion finalizes and the witness is rebuilt. The indexer cannot authorize arbitrary tree roots.

The relayer/sponsor funds permitted account creation and fees under separate limits. Sponsorship must not quietly fall back to the identifiable owner's withdrawal fee payment.

## Merchant payment and delivery

The wallet validates the full x402 V2 exact transaction: network, mint, amount, recipient ATA, transfer authority, fee payer, expiry, compute budgets and allowed instruction layout. Reject unrelated transfers, approvals and delegate changes.

The gateway validates the immutable quote/account/request binding and atomically claims the operation and signature before settlement. After finalized settlement, it records one financial event and either issues a credit pack once or authorizes one bounded service attempt. Paid retries return the existing status/result even after quote expiry.

| Payment option | Financial effect |
|---|---|
| Direct per-call x402 | One USDC payment; no prepaid debit |
| Credit-pack purchase | One USDC payment attributed to Shawn; one gateway issuance |
| Prepaid inference | Consume shared gateway credits and requesting agent usage allowance; no second USDC charge |

Mira's scripted demo uses a **direct private x402 content-package purchase**; its local-validator rehearsal uses a **fixture / mock provider**. Devnet run `2026-10-17-1eba868c` (before PR #3 merged) recorded the content-package withdrawal, a 300,000-base-unit merchant leg to the Veilo gateway and a live inference receipt; see the [demo checklist](./demo.md). Shawn demonstrates shared-credit replenishment; Prince may use the prepaid path.

## Marketplace settlement

A marketplace quote must bind the reviewed listing, runtime and payout versions, exact seller recipient, scope, network, mint, amount and expiry. The fresh signer pays that seller directly through x402 V2 exact. Execution waits for independently verified finality unless the quote is explicitly free. Quotes/receipts show a zero platform fee; seller earnings are finalized receipt history, not a platform balance. Gateway credits do not replace direct seller settlement.

Managed listings settle on the seller-host gateway profile to the listing's verified payout address, never through the operator's gateway merchant. Receipt-to-job uniqueness is enforced in the database (checked in the live RLS e2e script). Two devnet smokes settled directly to a seller's payout ATA with a publicly funded payer; a private-pool-funded hire is not yet run on devnet. One finalized receipt may fund one job and one earnings event. Refunds are separate seller-funded, finalized transfers to an owner-verified destination, cumulatively capped at the settled amount; failed delivery must remain visibly paid. Refund rules pass the live RLS e2e script; no live refund transfer is recorded. See the [marketplace guide](./marketplace.md).

## Devnet swap

An owner-approved swap is a private purchase whose second leg is an Orca swap instead of an x402 payment. It exists only on Solana devnet. On the earlier code, three swaps finalized on Solana devnet without error on 2026-10-17/18, before the October 19 hardening and agent-chosen-amount changes (relayer ledger; signatures `2ftArMuh…YsNp`, `3V3gg86d…KypN4`, `4XrL1GFp…PyNi6`, checked with `getSignatureStatuses`). The current code (hardened path, agent-chosen amount) is unit-tested in control, wallet, relayer and runner against fakes and has not yet run on devnet.

1. **Approval.** The owner approves one service, `swap:orca-devnet-sol-usdc` with SKU `swap-usdc-to-sol`, whose price is a **maximum per swap** (at most 5,000,000 base units). The pool (whirlpool `5GPCnpWwoDayCP5FVCJT1cS7dePufC5FrjPTVvPoUYnm`), direction (USDC to wrapped SOL), slippage (100 bps) and destination (`OWNER_RECOVERY_ADDRESS`) are fixed in code.
2. **Authorization.** The agent's input is exactly `{"amountUsdc": "<base units>"}`; any other field is refused. Control checks that the input matches the request digest and does not exceed the approved maximum, then prices the purchase at the requested amount, so the usual atomic reservation applies every cap to it. A swap is funded only through `private_x402`.
3. **Private funding.** The pool withdrawal funds a fresh wallet exactly as for an x402 purchase; the stored funding binding names the whirlpool and swap terms.
4. **Authority before signing.** Control records `sign_merchant` (rechecking policy and revocation) and asks the wallet to sign (`POST /fundings/:id/swap`).
5. **Wallet checks.** The wallet requires control's funding `finalized` and merchant `signed`. It reads the fresh wallet's USDC balance and swaps the **whole balance**, because anyone can send tokens to the public account and the same transaction must close it empty. It quotes on Orca, decodes the quoted `swapV2` and refuses it unless it sells exactly that balance of the fresh wallet's own USDC on the pinned whirlpool for the quoted minimum. It records `swap.signature_produced` before signing, so a crash never leads to a second signature.
6. **Relayer co-signing (`POST /swaps`).** The relayer accepts exactly five instructions: compute-unit limit; the sponsor creating the fresh wallet's wrapped-SOL account; one Orca `swapV2` on the pinned whirlpool; closing the wrapped-SOL account to the stated destination; closing the emptied USDC account with its rent to the sponsor. It verifies the fresh-wallet signature, checks the sponsor cap counting in-flight swaps at their worst case, and rechecks both the swap id and the cap inside the transaction that records it, so a concurrent retry neither re-broadcasts nor counts twice. Its crank marks a swap finalized only once it can read the fee from the finalized transaction.
7. **Settlement.** A finalized swap records the merchant leg finalized at the requested amount and the fulfilment delivered, with the minimum and estimated SOL output and the signature. A failed or expired swap moves the merchant leg to `expired_unsettled` and fulfilment to `abandoned`, and marks the purchase recoverable; the USDC stays in the fresh wallet. A wallet refusal (`recovery_required`) keeps the merchant leg `signed`, because the refusal alone does not prove whether a signature exists.

**Recovery of a swap that was never signed.** If the wallet holds no stored swap and no `swap.signature_produced` record for the purchase, owner recovery calls control's `POST /internal/wallet/purchases/:id/swap-not-signed` under the same lock that signs swaps. Control moves the merchant leg from `signed` to `expired_unsettled` with reason `swap_never_signed` and abandons fulfilment, and the wallet refuses to sign afterwards. The funded USDC is then recovered to `OWNER_RECOVERY_ADDRESS` like any funded wallet.

**Withdrawing approval** refuses new swaps at authorization and cancels a reserved swap whose proof was not released. A swap already released keeps settling or becomes recoverable.

**Privacy.** The swap is paid by a fresh wallet funded from the pool, but the SOL lands publicly at the owner's configured address, which links that swap to the owner.

**Known gaps (in code, not fixed):**

- The relayer does not reserve sponsor capacity for the later swap when it accepts the funding withdrawal, so a swap can be refused `BUDGET_EXCEEDED` after its funding settled; the USDC then stays recoverable in the fresh wallet.
- A failed swap's sponsor fee is recorded by the relayer but not passed to control's purchase record.
- In `services/relayer/src/withdrawals.ts`, a withdrawal fee is not recorded, and a recovery fee is recorded as 0, when `getTransaction` returns nothing.

## Recovery and failure handling

| Boundary | Required handling |
|---|---|
| Proof released, withdrawal outcome unknown | Keep exposure reserved; reconcile nullifier/chain state and proof expiry |
| Withdrawal finalized, merchant not signed | Track the funded wallet separately from pool notes; resume only within current policy |
| Merchant signed/submitted, response lost | Query the existing signature; do not automatically create another payment |
| Settlement finalized, issuance interrupted | Reconcile and issue the same pack once |
| Provider request outcome unknown | Record uncertain or paid-without-result; no blind retry without upstream idempotency |
| Agent stopped with a funded wallet | Recover only to the configured owner destination after conflicting authority is resolved |
| Swap leg never signed | Owner recovery records `swap_never_signed` in control, then recovers the funded USDC |
| Swap failed or expired on chain | Merchant leg `expired_unsettled`; USDC stays in the fresh wallet, recoverable by the owner |

Quote expiry, transaction last-valid block height and proof `valid_until_slot` are different bounds. Expiring a transaction does not necessarily invalidate a released proof that can be placed in another transaction. Release its reservation only after finalized chain evidence proves the authorization is no longer usable and no spend settled.

A public exit requires note ownership proof and the original refund authority. It must remain possible without approved-set membership; it reveals information and does not restore privacy. Test both original and change notes.

---

# Policy and accounting

For recorded verification and remaining checks, see [current status](./status.md).

## Permission tiers

| Tier | Permitted behavior | Still prohibited |
|---|---|---|
| Observe | Plan and explain proposals | Releasing spending proofs/signatures |
| Bounded automatic | Purchase without another approval when every applicable rule passes | Exceeding any cap or allowed service binding |
| Approval required | Request explicit owner approval for designated valid purchases | Using approval to bypass hard limits |
| Stopped | Reconcile existing operations | Releasing new spending authority |

Recovery and owner exit remain available through their separate authenticated paths. Editing policy is a distinct owner action. Structured policy changes create drafts that require owner activation. The dashboard can pre-fill limit fields from a plain-language description using a deterministic parser; it saves nothing by itself. Guests and the public viewer cannot edit policy.

## Marketplace approval and offline control

Specialist hiring keeps every local limit in force for specialist hires. A cloud identity session or cloud policy record cannot authorize spending: local control must install/acknowledge policy proposals and validate an approved seller plus immutable listing/payout/quote/runtime versions. A changed recipient or unapproved seller must stop locally. Concurrent hires share the same local allowance authority.

The required cloud connection uses authenticated, digest-bound, expiring requests initiated outbound by local control. New automatic spending pauses when control is offline; already released authority remains live exposure. Local approval bound to the operation, quote digest, recipient and total, owner-installed listing grants, concurrent-cap checks and revocation are implemented and unit-tested against fakes; lease and callback rules pass the live RLS e2e script. An offline-controller drill and a devnet run of these paths are still outstanding. See [triage](./marketplace-triage.md).

## Authorization algorithm

1. Authenticate the worker's bound workspace/agent, and validate supplied task ownership; do not trust an agent ID supplied in JSON.
2. Resolve the stable operation and immutable request/quote. Changed payload for the same operation conflicts before any payment.
3. Validate service origin, gateway identity, SKU, network, mint, recipient and quote bounds.
4. In a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction, recheck limits, status, policy version and note availability; create the unique operation/reservation.
5. Recheck policy and revocation epoch before proof release, withdrawal submission and merchant signing.
6. Reconcile finalized outcomes into durable financial events. Keep unknown outcomes reserved.

All writers use the same control authority/database. Multiple worker databases each checking their own caps cannot enforce a workspace cap.

## Independent limits

Every purchase must pass per-purchase, per-task lifetime, per-agent lifetime and rolling 24-hour, workspace lifetime and rolling 24-hour limits. Sponsor SOL fees and recoverable rent have separate bounds. Gateway usage has both scoped usage allowances and shared available credits.

Use integer amounts and decimal strings across APIs. Never compare financial amounts using floating point.

For each cash scope:

```text
available = limit - applicable settled cost - all active reservations
```

For rolling scopes, count settled costs within the preceding 24 hours **plus every live reservation**, even if it is older. A reservation crossing midnight or a rolling boundary does not release exposure.

For gateway credits:

```text
usable credits = issued - consumed - reserved
```

Cash spent, pool tokens, funded fresh-wallet principal, pending change, sponsor lamports, prepaid credits and provider dollars are different units/states. Never sum them into a single balance.

## Revocation and restoration

Pause/revoke must serialize against financial authority release. Already released proof/transaction material may settle until its bound expires; display that live exposure. Do not promise cancellation after release.

Recovering proven unpaid principal may restore eligible allowance. It does not refund a completed service or paid fees, and an external recovered balance does not create a private pool note. Re-entering the pool requires a new deposit.

Persist original settlement timestamps. A restart must not move old spending into a different window. Link refunds to their original expense; an expired expense cannot offset unrelated new rolling-window spending.

---

# Privacy and trust

For recorded verification and remaining checks, see [current status](./status.md).

## Intended protection

A shared note-based pool aims to remove the **explicit mapping from a particular deposited note to a withdrawal**. A local proof authorizes the withdrawal without naming the spent deposit. A fresh wallet then pays the merchant through standard x402, and private change remains in the pool.

This requires real on-chain proof verification and authenticated tree updates. Cosmetic address rotation, a trusted database withdrawal authorizer or an ordinary direct x402 payment does not establish this property.

## Which agent or wallet can someone identify?

| Question | Intended behavior |
|---|---|
| Can a public observer see the wallet that pays the merchant? | Yes. The fresh payment address, merchant, amount and timing remain public. |
| Does the withdrawal explicitly identify its original deposited note? | No, in a correctly implemented proof-based flow. Removing this explicit link is the privacy target. |
| Is an agent name or stable workspace ID published with each payment? | It must not be included in chain memos, proof public fields or withdrawal accounts. |
| Can the owner tell which agent spent money? | Yes. The local workspace keeps purchase attribution and outcomes. |
| Can the gateway link purchases or usage? | Yes. Its authenticated workspace account and request data provide off-chain linkage. |
| Is correlation impossible? | No. Small pools, distinctive amounts, funding trails, timing and network metadata can weaken privacy. |

Funding privacy and owner monitoring serve different audiences: the owner retains accountability while the chain omits an explicit deposit-to-withdrawal mapping. This is not a promise that every payment is anonymous to every observer.

## Visibility matrix

| Observer | Information visible in the intended design |
|---|---|
| Public-chain observer | Deposits, source addresses, payout wallets, amounts, mint, merchant payments, fees, timing, public exits and proof public inputs |
| Owner / local wallet service | Note secrets, local agent/task attribution, spending history, recovery metadata and signer material |
| Gateway operator | Authenticated workspace credit account, purchases, requests/prompts, usage, cached results and connection metadata |
| OpenRouter | Operator account, forwarded prompts and model/request metadata; internal workspace IDs are not forwarded by default |
| Relayer / RPC | Submitted public transactions and relevant connection/timing metadata; relayer should not receive note secrets |
| Approved-set / upgrade administrators | Disclosed powers to update approved membership or deployed program code, according to configuration |

Persistent gateway accounts deliberately link service usage off chain. The protocol does not hide prompts from the provider or establish network-level anonymity.

## Agent tools added after the merge

| Path | Who else sees what |
|---|---|
| Owner's model provider | Prompts, gathered page and connector text, outputs and any reference image. The provider bills and identifies the owner. |
| Read-only browsing | Each site sees a request from the runner host's address; control's audit keeps only the host. |
| Connectors (including CoinGecko market data) | The connector server sees the call arguments, such as coin ids. Calls are keyless and not private. |
| Result destinations | Telegram, Slack or Discord receive the task's saved outputs as plain text. |
| Devnet swap | A fresh wallet funded from the pool pays the swap, but the SOL lands publicly at `OWNER_RECOVERY_ADDRESS`, linking that swap to the owner's address. |

## Marketplace observer boundary — accepted v3.2 scope

Marketplace identity and job records create additional off-chain linkage. The marketplace operator, sellers, facilitators and model providers can see the buyer–seller relationship and plaintext job content they process. Supabase Web3 identity does not hide a buyer from the cloud operator. Private Storage and RLS restrict application access; they do not establish transaction or metadata anonymity.

Hosted seller execution must receive only permitted job data and no wallet secrets. Participant files are private and downloaded through short-lived signed links (checked in the live RLS e2e script). The required 30-day retention cleanup is not implemented. See [marketplace](./marketplace.md) and [acceptance gaps](./marketplace-triage.md).

## Correlation and anonymity limits

A small pool, one active participant, distinctive amounts, closely timed deposit/withdrawal/payment and common operator funding can make linkage plausible. Synthetic demo participants are not independent users. Approved-set size is membership information, not a measured anonymity score.

A separate fee sponsor reduces one obvious source link, but shared RPC endpoints and sponsor funding trails still permit correlation. Public exits and recovery transactions may reveal aggregate spending through subtraction.

Funding privacy does not guarantee anonymity against every observer. Security depends on correct circuits, proof verification, key handling and operational controls.

## Cryptography and setup trust

The current setup uses a deterministic local development powers-of-tau with public beacons. Its toxic waste is derivable: it is unsuitable for production funds. The development setup and unaudited verifier remain material trust risks even though M2 transactions finalized. See [known risks](../security/risks.md).

The Solana proof design uses BN254 Groth16, matching Poseidon parameters and canonical encodings across TypeScript, Circom and Rust.

The deployment manifest must pin circuit/compiler source, curve, hash parameters, public-input order, encoding/vector version, tree depths, proving/verifying-key hashes and setup provenance. Artifact mismatch stops proof generation. A malicious setup, buggy circuit/verifier or excessive upgrade authority can compromise funds/privacy.

Spend and public exit share one pool-scoped nullifier namespace. Bind withdrawal intent to the deployed program/pool, network, mint, exact destination, value/fees and on-chain expiry. The on-chain program reconstructs the intent; an off-chain annotation is insufficient.

## Operational privacy

- Keep note secrets and decryption/signer keys in the local wallet service, inaccessible to the runner.
- Do not put agent names, workspace IDs or gateway account identifiers in chain memos, withdrawal accounts or proof public fields.
- Minimize operator logs; redact secrets, authorization headers and private prompt content before evidence export.
- Retain enough authenticated purchase/result state to reconcile ambiguous outcomes; disclose retention and clean up only after outstanding operations resolve.
- Back up notes, change secrets, paths/rebuild data, fresh-wallet counters and pending operations with an encrypted snapshot. Wallet and control files are copied separately; quiesce writers for an operator snapshot and retain matching gateway state.

The owner machine remains trusted. Local proof generation does not protect secrets from a compromised host.

## Evidence needed before a privacy claim

Demonstrate a real deployed verifier, valid spend/change and owner exit, rejection of invalid proof/context/replay, public-input inspection for stable identifiers, and multiple clearly labeled test deposits. Include the metadata caveats above alongside that evidence. See [security matrix](../security/evidence.md) and [known risks](../security/risks.md).

---

# Running Veilo

Use your own wallet, deployment and provider accounts. A clean clone contains no author API keys, wallet keys or local state. [Current status](./status.md) records verification and remaining checks.

Provider-backed calls use the configured operator's real credits. Leave the real-inference budget at zero until you have configured your own account and spending limits. Do not copy an existing operator's `.env`, secret directory, databases or private keys, and do not point a new installation at their service credentials. Public program IDs, mint addresses and transaction receipts are not credentials.

## Marketplace setup (optional)

The local T00–T16 workspace runs without Supabase. To enable the marketplace, set the Supabase and marketplace variables from `.env.example` (see [configuration](../configuration.md#marketplace-service-and-dashboard)), apply `supabase/migrations/` to the project, enable the Supabase Web3 (Solana) sign-in provider, and run `pnpm setup:local` to create the seller-host and operator token files. `pnpm dev` then also starts the marketplace service and the seller host. A cloud session never authorizes a wallet spend.

```sh
pnpm test:marketplace-rls   # live identity/RLS/Storage checks; chain reads use a labeled fixture
pnpm marketplace:seed       # read-only plan; add --confirm to create the demo catalogue
```

The service key stays in the marketplace process only.

## Application quickstart

Use Node **24 LTS** (`>=22.14.0 <25`), **pnpm 10.34.6**, and Docker with a running Linux daemon. Native Rust, Solana, Anchor and circom are provided by the pinned Docker toolchain. Allow time/disk/network for the first image and proof builds.

From the repository root:

```sh
corepack enable pnpm
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm toolchain:build
pnpm setup:local
pnpm check:devnet
```

`setup:local` creates `.env` from `.env.example` if missing and local directories. It creates the wallet encryption root only when `OWNER_SERVICE_SECRET_PATH` is configured; it reports service credential paths but does not generate those credentials. Existing secrets are never replaced. Back up the encryption root separately; never commit it.

Edit `.env` locally using [configuration](../configuration.md): set `VEILO_OWNER_PUBKEY`, deployment manifest/program/pool values and role credential/key **paths**. Configure gateway merchant/ATA and facilitator fee payer consistently with the manifest. Missing bindings remain unbound/NOT_READY. For live inference only, the gateway needs an operator-funded OpenRouter key, allowlisted models and a nonzero bounded `OPERATOR_MAX_REAL_USD_MICRO`; devnet USDC cannot buy provider dollars.

For a new manual local stack, set `OWNER_SERVICE_SECRET_PATH=secrets/owner-service.secret`, `CONTROL_SERVICE_CREDENTIAL_PATH=secrets/control-service.credential`, `WALLET_SERVICE_CREDENTIAL_PATH=secrets/wallet-service.credential` and `RELAYER_SERVICE_CREDENTIAL_PATH=secrets/relayer-service.credential` in `.env`. Generate those three independent credentials without printing them (the directories already exist after setup):

```sh
node --input-type=module -e 'import {writeFileSync} from "node:fs"; import {randomBytes} from "node:crypto"; for (const role of ["control", "wallet", "relayer"]) writeFileSync(`secrets/${role}-service.credential`, randomBytes(32).toString("hex")+"\n", {flag:"wx", mode:0o600});'
pnpm setup:local
```

This command is for a fresh stack only and refuses existing files. Restore missing credentials for an existing ledger instead of resetting identities. On Windows restrict these credential files with owner-only ACLs; POSIX `mode` does not enforce a Windows ACL. The isolated `demo:run` creates its own credentials and does not use these manual-stack files.

```sh
pnpm demo:seed
pnpm check
pnpm test
pnpm dev
```

Seed policies start as drafts and seeding never issues credits. Open the dashboard at `http://localhost:3000`; it must match `VEILO_DASHBOARD_ORIGIN`, which binds the sign-in challenge and rejects mutating requests from another origin. `pnpm dev` starts the dashboard (Next.js dev server on webpack, port 3000) and control/runner/wallet/gateway/relayer on ports 4101–4105; with Supabase configured it also starts the marketplace (4106) and the seller host (4107 in `.env.example`), plus the optional carousel seller host when its `CAROUSEL_SELLER_*` settings are present. The runner reads public pages through an installed Chrome; set `RUNNER_BROWSER=off` if none is installed.

| Path | Screen |
|---|---|
| `/` | Public landing page |
| `/workspace` | Owner workspace: agents, policies, shared treasury, emergency stop |
| `/agents/new`, `/agents/<id>` | Create or configure an agent; the agent's chat, live steps and results |
| `/connectors` | Read-only MCP connectors attached to agents, and result destinations (Telegram, Slack, Discord) |
| `/outputs` | Saved results, editable content drafts and calendar |
| `/wallet` | Pool balance, deposit and exit, activity, recovery and the Agent swaps approval |
| `/settings` | The owner's AI model key and privacy limits |
| `/marketplace/…` | Open marketplace: workflows, role templates, create, tools, runs, jobs, seller console, agents, Local approval |

Older addresses redirect: `/activity` and `/recovery` to `/wallet`, `/privacy` to `/settings`, `/content` to `/outputs`, `/market` to `/marketplace`.

Sign in with the configured owner wallet, then review/activate workspace and agent policies. Add a model provider key in **Settings** so agents can do model work; without one only the operator-sponsored planning trial is available. How to approve swaps, attach CoinGecko market data and attach a reference image is in [agent workflows](./agents.md#owner-how-to-swaps-market-data-and-reference-images). Wallets listed in `VEILO_GUEST_PUBKEYS` sign in as guests: they can run agents within their policies (rate-limited by `VEILO_GUEST_RUNS_PER_HOUR`) but cannot configure, fund, recover or approve. `VEILO_PUBLIC_VIEW=1` adds a redacted read-only view without sign-in. The header toggles light/dark mode; without a choice the system setting applies. Run [deployment instructions](../deployment.md) to provision/fund roles and deploy a pool before attempting private purchases. A clean clone has no funded keys, proving keys, databases or provider credentials.

## Proofs, rehearsal and devnet recording

```sh
pnpm test:circuits
pnpm test:program
pnpm test:integration
pnpm demo:run -- --local-rehearsal
```

The integration suite needs the built program (`target/deploy/privacy_pool.so`) and manifest-compatible proving files (`circuits/build/`). The local rehearsal uses throwaway keys, loopback validator/facilitator and **fixture / mock provider**. It writes under ignored `work/demo-rehearsal/evidence/`; its signatures cannot be checked on a devnet explorer.

Devnet run `2026-10-17-1eba868c` and its export are committed under `artifacts/evidence/`. A new run must use its own run ID; do not reset operation IDs or reuse another run's state to manufacture a fresh result. The macOS operator checklist is in [deployment](../deployment.md).

For a new deployment, follow the [devnet runbook](../deployment.md#devnet-deployment-runbook-t09-m2), including key initialization, program-ID alignment/build and circuit manifest checks. Do not regenerate role or proving keys for an existing deployment. The deterministic development setup is unsuitable for production funds.

```sh
pnpm demo:run
# After readiness passes and operator budgets/policies are reviewed:
pnpm demo:run -- --execute --confirm
pnpm evidence:export
```

The first command is read-only and makes no inference call. Execution signs deposits, withdrawals/merchant payments and exit, and incurs bounded operator provider costs. Rerun the same execute command to resume recorded operations. The eight-step [demo script](./demo.md) gives expected records and screenshot placeholders.

The script starts isolated backend services; funded dashboard screenshots require a separately configured dashboard connected to those same run databases/service ports. A screenshot of another workspace is not evidence of this run.

## Backup and recovery

Quiesce service writers before `pnpm backup` for an operator snapshot: wallet and control files are copied separately. Use the encrypted wallet/control snapshot and keep `OWNER_SERVICE_SECRET_PATH` separately. Stop the wallet and other writers before `pnpm restore -- --file <encrypted-backup> --include-control`; retain the matching gateway ledger and credentials rather than resetting issued credits. Startup reconciliation blocks new authority until pending operations are resolved. See [configuration](../configuration.md) for the exact scope. A public exit/recovery can reveal spending/linkage and cannot cancel already released authority.

## Documentation site

The documentation has its own npm lockfile:

```sh
cd docs
npm ci
npm run dev
# Or build and preview:
npm run build
npm run preview
```

The default base is `/Veilo-agent-wallet/`; open the printed base URL. Use `DOCS_BASE=/ npm run build` for a domain root. The build generates `llms.txt`, its intentional compatibility alias `llms.text`, and `llms-full.txt`.

VitePress 1.6.4 uses a pinned Vite 6.4.4 override and Mermaid 12.2.0. Revalidate the build and browser behavior when changing these dependencies. A successful documentation build does not run application/security tests.

---

# Security self-assessment

Veilo separates agent planning from spending authority. This is a team self-assessment of the devnet prototype, not an independent audit. [Current status](../guide/status.md) and [execution evidence](../evidence.md) record what has been tested.

## Permission tiers

| Mode | Allowed behavior |
|---|---|
| Observe | Propose work; release no spending proof or signature |
| Bounded automatic | Execute only within all owner-approved limits and grants |
| Approval required | Obtain owner approval; hard limits still apply |
| Stopped | Reconcile existing operations; issue no new spending authority |

## Enforcement

| Component | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Local control | Authenticate requests, bind agent/workspace scope, reserve budgets atomically and enforce revocation |
| Local wallet | Encrypt notes and signing material, generate proofs, validate the complete payment or swap before signing |
| Solana pool | Verify proof/context, conserve value, reject duplicate nullifiers and bind payout/owner-exit destinations |
| Gateway | Bind quotes and requests, reconcile settlement, issue credits once and cache results |
| Marketplace | Isolate tenant records, protect quote/recipient versions, enforce one receipt per job and reject stale worker leases |
| Agent runner | Use restricted tools; treat third-party descriptions, pages and results as untrusted |

Owner sign-in uses a domain-bound wallet challenge with nonce and expiry. Browser mutations require CSRF protection. Worker credentials and internal service credentials have separate scopes. Marketplace sign-in never grants spending authority.

Note secrets, signer material and provider keys remain outside runner-readable state. Model keys are sealed locally. Browsing restricts public destinations, request size and page count. Personal MCP connections are owner-added to the local workspace without operator review. Supported read-oriented tools are discovered and digest-pinned; calls refuse tool drift and raw code execution. Shared marketplace connector publication retains operator review. Remote tool behavior remains trusted, so read-oriented naming is not proof of no side effects. These controls reduce exposure but do not eliminate prompt injection.

## Recovery and administrative trust

Released proofs and signed transactions count as live exposure until settlement or proven expiry. Retries reconcile the existing operation before issuing new authority. Backup restore requires matching wallet/control/gateway state and reconciliation.

The owner host is trusted. Budgets are service-enforced, not proof-enforced. Program upgrades can change enforcement; approval authorities can restrict private spending. Owner exit is independent of approved membership. The deterministic proof setup is suitable only for devnet test funds.

See [known risks](./risks.md) and [verification requirements](./evidence.md) for the remaining work. No claim of mainnet readiness, universal anonymity or independently reviewed security is made.

---

# Known risks

Veilo is an unaudited devnet prototype. These limits apply even when a transaction succeeds.

| Risk | Current boundary |
|---|---|
| Development proof setup | Deterministic setup has derivable toxic waste; use test funds only. Production requires suitable setup and independent review. |
| Trusted owner host | Compromise can expose notes/keys and bypass local budgets. Encryption at rest does not protect a compromised running service. |
| Public metadata | Deposits, payouts, amounts, merchant transfers, fees and timing remain public. Small pools provide weak privacy. |
| Administrative control | Upgrade authority can replace enforcement; approved-root authority can restrict private spending. Distinct keys do not prove independent operators. |
| Released payments | Pause/revoke stops new authority; already released transactions may settle. Uncertain operations require reconciliation. |
| Providers and prompts | Operators, sellers and model providers can see processed content and relationships. Restricted tools do not eliminate prompt injection. |
| Delivery and refunds | Direct prepayment is not escrow. Payment can succeed while delivery fails; refunds depend on seller action and chain verification. |
| Recovery | Missing change, inconsistent backups or reused signer material can lose funds or duplicate authority. Restore matching state and reconcile. |
| Swaps | Sponsor budget can be exhausted after pool funding. SOL delivered to the owner's public address creates a visible link. |
| Hosting and retention | Local process separation is not a hosted sandbox. Credential brokering and automatic content-retention cleanup are not implemented. |
| Availability | RPC, facilitator and provider outages can pause work or leave uncertain outcomes. Retries must remain bounded. |

[Current status](../guide/status.md) identifies pending live checks. [Dependency notices](../references/attribution.md) retain license-review gaps. Historical receipts and local tests do not establish production safety.

---

# Verification requirements

Use these checks when evaluating a release. Recorded results are on the [Evidence page](../evidence.md); outstanding product checks are in [current status](../guide/status.md). A requirement is not a passing result.

| Area | Required check |
|---|---|
| Network | Refuse mainnet, wrong mint and mismatched deployment/proving artifacts |
| Privacy pool | Accept valid spend/change; reject invalid proofs, altered intent, duplicate nullifiers and forged insertion |
| Permissions | Observe mode releases no funds; missing/replayed approval fails; all budgets hold under concurrency |
| Payment integrity | Reject altered amount/recipient/instructions; reuse one operation for retries; settle and fulfill once |
| Sessions and isolation | Reject wallet-challenge replay, CSRF, cross-workspace access and runner access to secrets |
| Revocation | Stop new authority while tracking already released proofs and signatures |
| Recovery | Reconcile lost replies and restarts without duplicate debits; restore change and signer state |
| Marketplace | Protect tenant data, immutable quotes, receipt uniqueness, worker leases, refunds and result downloads |
| Paid delivery | Pair real devnet seller settlement with the resulting output; distinguish fixtures and live providers |
| Owner withdrawal | Bind the original refund authority and verify the finalized return destination |

Every result should name the tested source, deployed program/artifacts, environment, date, scenario, expected/observed outcome and failures/skips. For payments, include the full funding and settlement signatures, amount, recipient and delivered result. Local-validator signatures must never be labelled as devnet receipts.

Unit tests, local-validator integration, live database checks and devnet transactions establish different things. None substitutes for independent security review. [Marketplace verification](../guide/marketplace-triage.md) summarizes its remaining end-to-end checks.

## Diagram: architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  owner["Owner dashboard<br/>Create agents and set rules"]
  runner["Agent runner<br/>Propose a resource purchase"]
  control["Control service<br/>Check policy and reserve budget"]
  wallet["Wallet service<br/>Private notes, proofs and signing"]
  ledger[(Durable allowance ledger)]
  owner -->|job| runner
  owner -->|policy and approval| control
  runner -->|purchase request| control
  control -->|record reservation| ledger
  control -->|approved operation| wallet
```

## Diagram: private-funding

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  wallet["Local wallet service<br/>Encrypted notes and bound proof"]
  relay["Relayer and indexer<br/>Submit and track public state"]
  pool["Solana pool program<br/>Verify proof and spend note"]
  fresh["Fresh payment wallet<br/>Per-purchase payout and payment"]
  merchant["Merchant token account<br/>Receive ordinary x402 payment"]
  wallet -->|withdrawal proof| relay
  relay --> pool
  pool -->|PDA vault payout| fresh
  fresh -->|facilitator-settled transfer| merchant
```

## Diagram: service-delivery

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  control["Owner control service<br/>Bound quote and operation"]
  gateway["Veilo service gateway<br/>Payment checks and result cache"]
  facilitator["x402 facilitator<br/>Verify and settle merchant payment"]
  credits[(Shared gateway credit ledger)]
  provider["OpenRouter or data adapter<br/>Bounded service delivery"]
  control -->|authenticated request| gateway
  gateway -->|payment payload| facilitator
  facilitator -->|settlement result| gateway
  gateway -->|credit pack or prepaid usage| credits
  gateway -->|operator-funded inference or data| provider
  gateway -->|result and status| control
```

## Diagram: payment

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor Owner
  participant Agent
  participant Control
  participant Wallet
  participant Pool as Relayer / Pool
  participant Gateway
  participant Facilitator
  participant Provider
  Owner->>Control: Activate bounded policy
  Agent->>Control: Request approved purchase
  Control->>Gateway: Stable operation and request digest
  Gateway-->>Control: Immutable bound quote
  Control->>Control: Atomically check caps and reserve
  Control->>Wallet: Authorized operation and policy epoch
  Wallet->>Wallet: Persist fresh signer, recheck policy, prove locally
  Wallet->>Pool: Release bound withdrawal proof
  Pool->>Pool: Verify, consume nullifier, fund fresh wallet, queue change
  Pool-->>Wallet: Finalized withdrawal
  Wallet->>Wallet: Recheck epoch and all merchant instructions
  Wallet->>Gateway: Submit bound x402 payment
  Gateway->>Gateway: Validate and claim operation / signature
  Gateway->>Facilitator: Settle exact merchant payment
  Facilitator-->>Gateway: Finalized settlement evidence
  Gateway->>Gateway: Persist one payment event
  alt Credit pack
    Gateway->>Gateway: Issue shared credits once
  else Direct inference purchase
    Gateway->>Provider: One bounded operator-funded attempt
    Provider-->>Gateway: Real output or uncertain outcome
    Gateway->>Gateway: Persist result or paid-without-result
  end
  Gateway-->>Control: Existing purchase status / result
  Control-->>Agent: Save output and attributed cost
  Note over Control,Gateway: Retry same operation: reconcile or return cache, never blindly pay again
```

## Diagram: marketplace

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  buyer["Buyer / owner agent<br/>Discover and propose a specialist"]
  cloud["Marketplace — planned<br/>Supabase identity, catalogue, jobs and private files"]
  control["Owner-local control<br/>Approve seller, check limits, reserve and reconcile"]
  wallet["Owner-local wallet<br/>Note secrets, proof and constrained signing"]
  pool["Existing Solana pool<br/>Proof-authorized fresh-wallet funding"]
  exact["Ordinary public x402 V2 exact<br/>Verified seller recipient"]
  seller["Reviewed seller runtime — planned<br/>Run only after verified finality or explicit free quote"]
  result["Private deliverable and finalized receipt<br/>One payment, one job, one earnings event"]
  buyer --> cloud
  control <-->|"Local control initiates outbound connection<br/>Authenticated, digest-bound, expiring requests"| cloud
  control -->|"Local authority only"| wallet
  wallet --> pool
  pool --> exact
  exact --> seller
  seller --> result
  result --> cloud
```
